title: Role Transition and Backfill Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood's standard process for role transitions (promotions, lateral moves, and exits) and backfills. It consolidates manager, people-ops, and team responsibilities to minimize service disruption, preserve institutional knowledge, and accelerate handovers. Use this as the canonical checklist and timeline for any role change that impacts active workstreams or customer commitments.

When to use this playbook:
- A team member accepts a new internal role (promotion or transfer).
- A headcount is vacated (resignation, termination, or extended leave).
- A manager decides to add or reshape a role and needs to recruit a backfill.

Goals and success criteria:
- Primary services maintain customer SLOs during transition (no >10% sustained latency regression attributable to staffing change).
- Handover completed with no critical knowledge gaps: at least one runbook, one paired session, and an up-to-date task list shared.
- New hire or transferee productive in core duties within their first 30 days (progress tracked by manager checkpoints).

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- People-ops: approve hiring or role change, update Headcount tracker, run offer and onboarding logistics, coordinate cross-team communications.
- Hiring manager / New manager: define role scope, create/update role profile and success criteria, lead interview and selection, run first 90-day plan and weekly 1:1s.
- Outgoing individual (if applicable): deliver handover artifacts, complete knowledge-transfer sessions, tag relevant docs and claims.
- Team peers / domain SME: coauthor runbooks, participate in shadowing, take short-term ownership of critical queues.
- Eng-platform / Infra: (as needed) support access changes, escalate observed regressions to eng-sre.

Standard timeline and checkpoints (typical for voluntary internal transfer):
1) Pre-transition (4+ weeks before move)
   - Manager notifies People-ops and updates internal Headcount tracker.
   - Draft role profile and 90-day success criteria (document link).
   - Identify interim coverage plan for critical on-call or production queues.

2) Announcement & recruitment (3–4 weeks before move)
   - People-ops publishes role opening internally (Greenhouse + internal channel).
   - Manager assembles interview panel and assigns scorecard owners.

3) Selection & offer (1–3 weeks)
   - Offer approved by People-ops; compensation matched to band and precedent.
   - Effective date and reporting line confirmed.

4) Handover period (2 weeks before -> 2 weeks after transfer)
   - Outgoing contributor prepares the Handover Package (see "Handover Package" section).
   - Three paired sessions scheduled (shadowing, runbook walkthrough, escalation scenarios).
   - Access & repo permissions reviewed; entitlement changes requested by manager via the Access request form.

5) Post-transition (0–90 days after transfer)
   - Manager runs 1:1 cadence: weekly for first 30 days, then biweekly until day 90.
   - People-ops schedules 30/60/90 check-ins and nudges training enrollments (compliance, security, platform).

Handover Package (required artifacts) — manager must confirm completion:
- Role summary: one-paragraph scope, primary metrics, and current OKRs.
- Critical systems list: service names, on-call rotations, runbook links, pager severity thresholds.
- Current work-in-progress: JIRA ticket list (links), expected owners, and blockers.
- Key contacts matrix: internal SMEs, external partners, customer owners.
- Access matrix snapshot: repos, dashboards, test environments, and credential handoff notes.
- Known risks & mitigation: backlog items that might cause regressions and proposed owners.

Handover Package template (copy-paste snippet):

--- Handover Summary ---
Role: {ROLE_NAME}
Effective date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
Primary objective: {short description}
Key services: {service-a, service-b}
On-call coverage: {yes/no}  Pager escalation: {SEV1 contact}

WIP tickets:
- [PROJECT-123] Owner: @user  ETA: 2026-03-01
- [PROJECT-456] Owner: @user  ETA: 2026-04-12

Runbooks and dashboards:
- Service A runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/service-a-runbook
- SLO dashboard: Grafana /dashboards/slo-service-a

Known risks:
- Data-migration scheduled for Q2; requires DBA involvement.

---

Communication and announcement checklist:
- Draft public announcement for team and cross-functional partners.
- Update org chart and team page on Confluence.
- Add calendar hold for handover sessions (30–60 min each).
- Notify customers where the role change affects primary contacts (CS/AM to coordinate).

Temporary coverage patterns (examples):
- Short leave (<4 weeks): assign peer as "interim owner" with explicit escalation rights; no new hires unless capacity permanent.
- Extended vacancy (>8 weeks): open backfill requisition with People-ops; consider contractor for critical production work.
- Promotion creating new vacancy: prioritize internal candidate pool to reduce knowledge transfer time.

Interview and evaluation guidance for backfill hires:
- Scorecards must reflect the updated role profile and competency map.
- Include at least one practical exercise or code/design review relevant to the role.
- Interview panel should contain a peer, a manager, and a product or SRE stakeholder where applicable.
- Use rubric: Technical (40%), Systems & Docs (20%), Collaboration & Culture (20%), Problem Solving (20%).

Access and tooling steps (quick reference):
- Greenhouse: create requisition and tag with team, hiring manager, and urgency.
- Okta/SCIM: request role entitlement changes at least 3 business days before effective date.
- Lattice: move performance plan to new manager after transfer; people-ops will coordinate.
- Confluence: update team page and copy runbook ownership to new assignee.

Manager checklist (signed off before day 0):
- [ ] Handover Package uploaded to Confluence.
- [ ] Three paired sessions scheduled and recorded.
- [ ] Interview panel assembled and scorecard ready (for backfill).
- [ ] Access changes requested and temporary credentials issued if needed.
- [ ] Customer and partner notifications drafted.
- [ ] Temporary escalation path assigned and documented.

Risk mitigation playbooks (if transition impacts SLOs):
- If latency or error rate increases >5% above baseline after transition, escalate to eng-sre and invoke the "production-continuity" runbook.
- For high-severity incidents during handover, senior manager must be looped in within 60 minutes.

Templates and examples (links):
- Example Handover Package: /confluence/company-handbook/examples/handover-samples
- Manager communication template: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/role-change-announcement

FAQ (common manager questions):
Q: How long should knowledge transfer sessions be?
A: Aim for three 60-minute deep dives plus shorter 30-minute follow-ups. Record sessions when possible and post notes.

Q: What if the role requires specialized hardware or access?
A: Begin entitlement requests early (Okta + infra tickets). For on-prem hardware, engage eng-infra and schedule a provisioning lead time of 2–3 weeks.

Q: Should we always backfill a promoted role?
A: Not always. Managers should review prioritization with their director and People-ops based on capacity, OKR impact, and budget constraints.

Escalation contacts:
- People-ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Eng SRE on-call: pager duty (see on-call roster)
- HR employment questions: hr@redwood.ai

Appendix: Example 30/60/90 checkpoints (manager guidance)
- Day 30: Core service ownership demonstrated (can triage common SEVs), initial OKR intake complete.
- Day 60: Independent ownership for routine deployments and service health, engagement with cross-functional partners established.
- Day 90: Fully operational in role; evidence-based 90-day review and calibration with People-ops.

Document maintenance:
This playbook is owned by People-ops and will be reviewed annually or after every major reorg. Submit suggestions or edge-case reports to the People-ops Confluence page.
